answer: To resist Sybil attacks, we use Stake-Bonded TPM Attestation. First, agents must lock $50,000 in collateral. Second, a hardware enclave generates a unique, non-copyable cryptographic signature. Third, the network validates this identity against a basalt-hard registry. This prevents a cost spiral where attackers attempt to mass-produce fake identities, as each requires $50,000 and 72 hours of verification. Any fraudulent ripple in the network is instantly crushed by the weight of these bonds. It is like trying to carve a canyon through granite with a single wooden spoon.
